Team

The people behind the research

Members

Lea M. Ibele

CNRS researcher

Lea studied Chemistry at the University of Vienna. In 2022, she obtained a PhD in theoretical chemistry from Durham University under the supervision of Prof. Basile Curchod. Their thesis was focused on developing benchmark systems for nonadiabatic dynamics and computational time-resolved spectroscopy. In her postdoctoral experience, working with Dr. Federica Agostini at Paris-Saclay University, she focused on method development based on the exact factorization. In January 2025, Lea joined the Institute of Radical Chemistry at Aix Marseille University as a CNRS researcher (chargée de recherche). She likes to spend her free time rock climbing and disovering the best vegetarian food spots. Lea is passionate about contemporary performance art and intersectional queer feminist political movements.

Carlo Albani

PhD student since 2025

Carlo studied Chemistry at the University of Bologna, where in 2025 he obtained his MSc in Photochemistry and Molecular Materials. His master’s thesis focused on the development of PULSE-PySpawn, a software package for simulating transient absorption spectra within the Ab Initio Multiple Spawning (AIMS) framework. In November 2025 he started his PhD at the Institute of Radical Chemistry at Aix-Marseille University, where he is working on adapting enhanced sampling techniques to excited states, with the aim of sampling excited-state potential energy surfaces to model fluorescence. Outside (and inside) the lab, he spends most of his days listening to music, which accompanies him through every simulation and every line of code.

Anna Lamancová

PhD student since 2026

Anna obtained her bachelor’s degree in Chemistry from the University of Chemistry and Technology, Prague. Her bachelor’s thesis focused on dative bonding and its stability in solution. She then completed a master’s degree in Physical Chemistry at the same university, working under the supervision of Dana Nachtigallová on predicting the rotational half-lives of molecular rotors. Her PhD research focuses on conical intersections and how they can be shaped using spectroscopic techniques, combining computational chemistry with experimental collaboration. Outside of research, she spends most of her free time with her daughter and enjoy staying active. She used to compete in orienteering at a high level, and more recently has developed an interest in strength training. When she needs to slow down and unwind, she enjoys embroidery.
